trials.name: POLARIS-AD
trials.primary_endpoint: Clinical Dementia Rating Scale - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB)

trials.name: Bio-Hermes
trials.primary_endpoint: Measurement of blood-based biomarker levels (Beta-Amyloid, Phospho-Tau, Neurofilament Light Chain)

trials.name: BioFINDER-2
trials.population: Cognitively unimpaired individuals and patients with cognitive impairment

related_evidence.description: Peer-reviewed multicenter validation of the Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio in 499 symptomatic Alzheimer's disease patients (the dataset used for FDA clearance).

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence for the Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio is robust, grounded in a 499-patient multicenter validation study published in Alzheimer's & Dementia in July 2026. Rather than a single standalone trial, the FDA clearance was based on pooling plasma samples from established cohorts including the POLARIS-AD phase 3 trial, the BioFINDER-2 study, and the Bio-Hermes database. The data verified high diagnostic accuracy—91.8% positive predictive value and 97.3% negative predictive value against gold-standard CSF/PET markers—meaning the blood test is a highly reliable alternative to invasive procedures for early amyloid detection. However, the evidence also confirms a substantial 19.6% indeterminate result rate, reinforcing the FDA's warning that the blood ratio cannot function as a standalone diagnostic and will still require roughly one in five patients to undergo confirmatory testing.
discrepancies: The press release cites a 91.7% positive agreement, whereas the final peer-reviewed publication of the pivotal dataset reports a 91.8% positive predictive value (PPV); these are practically identical but rely on slightly different clinical terminology.

The FDA document describes the data simply as a 'multi-center study of 499 cognitively impaired adults,' omitting that this was actually a retrospective pooled validation of samples aggregated from several different observational cohorts and clinical trials (POLARIS-AD, Bio-Hermes, BioFINDER-2) rather than a newly registered de novo diagnostic trial.
